full_text_zh:
[P1] 走为上计

[P2] 春秋时期，晋国发生了内乱，公子重耳
只好四处逃亡。有一次，重耳逃到了楚国。楚王把他当作贵客，摆了酒宴招待他。他们一边喝酒，一边聊天。忽然，
楚王问重耳："如果有一天，你回到晋国，
当上了国君，要怎么报答我呢？"

[P3] 重耳想了想说："奴隶仆从、珍宝丝绸，大王您多得数不清。珍禽奇兽、羽毛兽皮，是您楚地的特产。晋国哪有什么奇珍异宝，值得献给大王呢？"
楚王大笑一声，追问道："公子太谦虚了。虽然我什么也不缺，但你也应该回赠一些礼物，表达你的谢意吧？"

[P4] 重耳也笑了笑，回答说："要是托您的福，我回晋国做了国君，将来晋国和楚国交战的时候，我一定命令军队，先退九十里，以报答您的情谊。" 楚王听后，觉得重耳很了不起，就客客气气地把他送出了楚国。后来，重耳真的做了晋国国君，他就是晋文公。

[P5] 那时候，诸侯国之间经常打仗。有一年，为了争夺中原霸主的地位，楚国摆开阵势，准备和晋国大战一场。楚军由令尹子玉率领，分成左军、中军、右军三路，来势汹汹。晋军由晋文公亲自统率，准备迎敌。

[P6] 后退九十里？
两国的军队剑拔弩张，眼看一场大战就要打起来。可让大家没想到的是，晋文公却下令："全军后退九十里！"他还派了人，前往秦国和齐国求助。
许多晋军将士心里不服气："楚军是臣子领兵，而我们是国君领兵；晋国的国君遇到楚国的臣子，却要后退避让，真是奇耻大辱啊！"

[P7] 晋文公却说："当年，如果没有楚王的帮助，我回不了晋国，也做不了国君。后退九十里，是因为我要说话算数，知恩图报。而且，楚军远道而来，再行军九十里，会更加疲劳，我们不是更容易取胜吗？"

[P8] 楚军将领也在猜测："晋军为什么还没开战就后退呢？是不是前方有埋伏？"他们纷纷劝说子玉，不要追赶，撤军回国。
子玉不听劝说，猛甩鞭子，一马当先地追了出去："晋军这是害怕了。三军收起营帐，全力追击。"

[P9] 晋军一直退到了城濮。城濮紧挨着晋国，粮草运过来很方便。齐国和秦国的大军也来到了城濮附近，助战晋国。
晋军在城濮安下营，扎了寨。大军的几千营火，就像天上的星星一样，在黑沉沉的夜色中闪烁。
楚军快马加鞭，追到城濮，也在一个小山坡下建好了营寨。

[P10] 子玉迫不及待地派出使者，向晋文公下了一封充满挑衅意味的战书：请晋军将士和楚军将士进行一场决斗，晋侯可以在战车上观战，我也陪您开开眼。晋文公毫不畏惧，回信说：贵国的帮助，我从来没有忘记。我军后退到这里，贵国还不愿意退兵，那就请准备好战车和兵器，明天我们在战场上相见！

[P11] 晋军有七百辆战车，战马已经套上了马铠，拴上了绳索，装备齐全。晋文公还命士兵砍了山上的树木，做成了武器。第二天天刚亮，随着“咚咚”的战鼓声响起，决战开始了！子玉得意地说：“今天一定要灭掉晋军！”他先派出了右军，去进攻晋军。

[P12] 楚国右军的战车飞一样冲向晋军，步兵们挥着长戟，猛冲猛杀。晋军手中拿的，却是昨天刚刚削出来的木棍，他们边打边退，最后竟然一头钻进了昏暗的树林。楚军紧追不放，也跟着钻了进去。忽然，从树林里冲出了一队战车，车前的战马身上，披着棕黄色的虎皮。虎皮战马奔来，就像老虎扑过来一样。楚军的战马吓得扬蹄乱奔，士兵也吓得转头就跑。

[P13] 楚国右军吃了个大败仗，全部被抓。晋文公却悄悄派士兵穿上楚军的衣服，去向子玉报告好消息："右军胜利了，元帅赶快派兵，消灭晋军。"子玉登上战车，向晋军看去。只见黄色的尘土漫天飞舞，他大笑起来："晋军一定是想逃跑，左军赶快追击。"

[P14] 晋军打着帅旗，引马飞快地撤退。楚国左军紧跟在后面，又钻进了晋军的伏击圈，很快就被消灭得一干二净。
原来，那黄色的尘雾，是晋军在马尾巴上绑了树枝，来回奔跑，从地上扫起来的，就是为了引楚军追上来。

[P15] 等子玉率领中军赶过来的时候，晋军立刻从四面八方冲出来，将他们团团围住。
子玉这才发现，右军、左军都已经战败了。
他带着中军拼命突围，这才保住性命，灰溜溜地回了楚国。

[P16] 在这场城濮之战中，晋文公三次主动后退，都不是想逃跑，而是想要寻找更有利的作战地点，把敌人引进自己的伏击圈。
当我们遇到强敌的时候，后退回避，寻找有利位置，也许是更好的计策，这就叫“走为上计”。
full_text_en:
[P1] Retreat is the best strategy.

[P2] In the Spring and Autumn period, there was an internal conflict in the State of Jin, and Prince Chong'er
had to flee everywhere. Once, Chong'er escaped to the State of Chu. The King of Chu treated him as a guest of honor, holding a banquet for him. They drank wine and chatted. Suddenly,
the King of Chu asked Chong'er: "If one day you return to Jin and
become its ruler, how will you repay me?"

[P3] Chong Er thought for a moment and said, "Slaves, servants, precious jewels, and silk—Your Majesty has more than you can count. Rare birds, exotic animals, feathers, and animal skins are specialties of your Chu territory. What rare treasures could Jin possibly have to offer Your Majesty?"
King Chu burst into laughter and asked, "You're too modest, young lord. Although I lack nothing, you should still give me a gift to express your gratitude, don't you think?"

[P4] Chong Er smiled and replied, "If I am fortunate enough to return to Jin and become its ruler, when Jin and Chu fight in the future, I will surely order my army to retreat ninety li first, as a way to repay your kindness." After hearing this, the King of Chu thought Chong Er was remarkable, and politely sent him away from Chu. Later, Chong Er truly became the ruler of Jin, and he was known as Duke Wen of Jin.

[P5] At that time, the feudal states often fought each other. One year, in order to compete for dominance over the Central Plains, Chu deployed its troops and prepared to fight a major battle against Jin. Chu's army, led by the Minister of War Zi Yu, was divided into three divisions: the left, center, and right armies, advancing with great force. Jin's army, personally commanded by Duke Wen of Jin, prepared to meet the enemy.

[P6] Retreat ninety li?
Armies from both states were poised for battle, and a great war seemed imminent. But to everyone's surprise, Duke Wen of Jin gave the order: "The entire army will retreat ninety li!" He also sent envoys to seek help from the states of Qin and Qi.
Many Jin soldiers were indignant: "The Chu army is led by a minister, while we are led by our sovereign. How can the ruler of Jin retreat and yield to a minister of Chu? This is truly a great shame and humiliation!"

[P7] Duke Wen of Jin said: "Years ago, without the help of the King of Chu, I could not have returned to Jin or become its ruler. Retreating ninety li is because I must keep my word and repay kindness. Moreover, the Chu army has come from afar; if they march another ninety li, they will be even more exhausted. Wouldn't that make it easier for us to win?"

[P8] The Chu army commanders were guessing: "Why is the Jin army retreating before even engaging in battle? Could there be an ambush ahead?" They urged Zi Yu not to pursue and to withdraw back to the homeland.
Zi Yu ignored their advice, whipped his horse hard, and charged forward: "The Jin army is afraid. The three armies, pack up the camps, and pursue with all force!"

[P9] The Jin army retreated all the way to Chengpu. Chengpu is close to the Jin state, making it very convenient to transport supplies. The large armies of Qi and Qin also arrived near Chengpu to assist the Jin.
The Jin army set up camp and established their encampment in Chengpu. The thousands of campfires of the army, like stars in the sky, flickered in the dark night.
The Chu army galloped swiftly, chased to Chengpu, and also set up their camp at the foot of a small hill.

[P10] Zi Yu, unable to wait any longer, sent an envoy to Duke Wen of Jin with a provocative challenge: 'Let the soldiers of Jin and Chu fight a duel. The Duke of Jin may watch from his war chariot, and I will accompany you to see it.' Duke Wen of Jin, undaunted, replied: 'I have never forgotten your country's kindness. My army has retreated to this point, yet your country still refuses to withdraw. Then please prepare your chariots and weapons—we shall meet on the battlefield tomorrow!'

[P11] The Jin army had seven hundred war chariots. The warhorses were already fitted with armor and harnessed with ropes, fully equipped. Duke Wen of Jin also ordered his soldiers to cut down trees from the mountains and turn them into weapons. The next morning, just as dawn broke, the battle began with the sound of 'dong dong' war drums! Zi Yu said proudly, 'Today, I will surely destroy the Jin army!' He first sent out his right wing to attack the Jin forces.

[P12] The right wing of the Chu army charged toward the Jin forces like flying, with infantry swinging long halberds, fiercely attacking. The Jin soldiers, holding only wooden sticks freshly carved the day before, fought while retreating, and eventually plunged into a dark forest. The Chu army pursued relentlessly, following them into the woods. Suddenly, a group of war chariots burst out from the forest, their warhorses draped in tawny tiger skins. The tiger-skinned horses galloped forward like tigers pouncing. The Chu horses were frightened, rearing and galloping wildly, and the soldiers turned and fled in panic.

[P13] Chu's right army suffered a major defeat and was completely captured. Jin Wen Gong secretly sent soldiers dressed in Chu army uniforms to report good news to Zi Yu: "The right army has won! Commander, quickly send troops to destroy the Jin army." Zi Yu climbed onto his war chariot and looked toward the Jin army. Seeing yellow dust swirling in the sky, he laughed: "The Jin army must be trying to escape. Left army, quickly pursue and attack!"

[P14] The Jin army, flying their banner, quickly retreated with their horses. The Chu left army followed closely behind and fell right into the Jin army's ambush, being completely wiped out.
Originally, that yellow dust was created by the Jin army tying branches to the tails of their horses, running back and forth to sweep up dirt from the ground—specifically to lure the Chu army into chasing them.

[P15] When Zi Yu led the central army to arrive, the Jin forces immediately charged out from all directions, surrounding them.
Zi Yu then realized that the right and left wings had already been defeated.
He led the central army in a desperate breakout, barely saving his life, and returned to Chu in disgrace.

[P16] In this Battle of Chengpu, Duke Wen of Jin retreated three times voluntarily, not to flee, but to find a more favorable position and lure the enemy into his ambush.
When we encounter a strong enemy, retreating to avoid confrontation and seeking a favorable position may be a better strategy—this is called 'retreating is the best strategy.'
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 页面标题为“走为上计”，配图是一位穿着古装、表情惊慌、正在逃跑的男子，暗示在危急情况下选择逃跑是明智之举。
[P2] 本页描绘了春秋时期公子重耳流亡至楚国，楚王以贵客之礼款待他，并在酒宴上询问他若日后成为国君将如何报答自己。
[P3] 重耳在楚国受楚王款待，面对楚王询问日后如何报答，他谦逊地表示晋国并无奇珍异宝可献；楚王大笑后，继续追问应如何回赠礼物以表谢意。
[P4] 重耳在楚国宴会上承诺，若日后成为晋君，将在晋楚交战时退兵九十里以报答楚王。楚王赞赏其气度，将其礼送出境。后来重耳果然成为晋文公。
[P5] 本页描绘了春秋时期楚国与晋国即将开战的场景，楚军由令尹子玉率领，分三路进攻，晋军则由晋文公亲自统率迎敌。
[P6] 本页描绘了晋楚两国军队对峙，晋文公下令全军后退九十里，引发晋军将士不满，认为此举有损国君尊严。
[P7] 晋文公在晋楚对峙时，向将士解释后退九十里是为了信守承诺、报答楚王昔日恩情，并认为此举可使楚军疲惫，利于取胜，但将士们对此表示不满。
[P8] 楚军将领怀疑晋军后退是因有埋伏，劝子玉勿追，但子玉不听，认为晋军畏惧，遂率军全力追击。
[P9] 晋军退至城濮安营扎寨，齐国和秦国军队前来助战；楚军紧追不舍，在城濮附近的小山坡下也建好了营寨，双方对峙。
[P10] 楚国令尹子玉向晋文公发出挑战，要求双方将士决斗，晋文公则回信表明自己铭记楚国旧恩，但因楚军不退兵，双方将在战场上决一胜负。
[P11] 晋楚两军在城濮对峙，晋军准备充分，楚军将领子玉率军进攻，决战正式开始。
[P12] 楚国右军猛攻晋军，晋军以木棍抵抗并退入树林，楚军紧追不舍。突然，晋军从树林中派出披着虎皮的战马战车，楚军战马受惊，士兵慌乱逃窜。
[P13] 楚国右军战败被俘，晋文公派士兵假扮楚军向子玉报捷，子玉误判晋军溃败，命令左军追击。
[P14] 晋军假装撤退，用马尾绑树枝制造尘雾引诱楚军左军追击，使其落入伏击圈并被全歼。
[P15] 子玉率中军赶来时，晋军四面围攻，他发现左右两军已败，只得率中军突围，最终侥幸逃生，灰溜溜返回楚国。
[P16] 本页通过文字总结城濮之战中晋文公三次后退的战略意图，并引申出“走为上计”的智慧，画面描绘楚军溃败、士兵狼狈逃窜的场景。
